Class Histogram

java.lang.Object
imageproof.Histogram
public class Histogram extends Object
Turns an image into gray values (0 to 255) and a 256-bin histogram. This is the first step of the analysis.

Rules:

  • gray = round(0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B)
  • transparent pixels are mixed onto a white background first
  • gray images use their stored sample directly (16-bit is scaled to 0-255)

A histogram counts how many pixels have each gray value. It is normalized by dividing each count by the total, so the 256 bins add up to 1. Comparison compares two such histograms.

    • entropy

      public static double entropy(double[] p)
      Shannon entropy in bits: -sum(p[i] * log2(p[i])). 0 means one gray value only. 8 means all 256 values are equally common.
      Parameters:
      p - normalized histogram (256 values)
      Returns:
      the entropy, 0 to 8
